subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 07, 2026
body:
Grml 2026.09 has arrived, bringing kernel 7.3-rc2 and fresh packages to AcreetionOS users worldwide. The new GRVM release includes critical security hardening and performance improvements that align perfectly with our focus on stability and privacy. This is the kind of update that keeps the community moving forward without unnecessary friction.

Development
The Grml 2026.09 release introduces several key changes that benefit AcreetionOS users directly. The kernel preppatch 7.3-rc2 brings bug fixes and optimizations that reduce system overhead during boot. Users can find detailed release notes on the changelog at acreetionos.org/changelog.html, where every commit is tracked transparently. The new GRVM packages are available through the standard AcreetionOS download portal at acreetionos.org/flash.html for seamless installation. These updates reflect months of careful work by the development team to maintain a reliable foundation.

Community
Our community continues to contribute meaningfully to the ecosystem. Natalie Spiva recently pushed the bash2bat conversion script, enabling easier migration to newer shell environments while preserving backward compatibility. The team also added MCP stdio servers in natalie/us-infra-hub, expanding interoperability with emerging AI infrastructure tools. For deeper exploration of these changes, see the full discussion on the wiki at acreetionos.org/wiki.html. The collaborative spirit remains strong as developers share knowledge freely.

Tip of the Day
To stay ahead of security updates, enable automatic dependency scanning in your CI pipeline. The configure secret detection feature in natalie/my-politecal-stances helps catch accidental credential leaks before they reach production. Check the latest guidance in the documentation at acreetionos.org/docs.html for step-by-step setup instructions. Proactive security habits protect everyone on the platform.
